system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
Shame on . To this day Spotify is unable to rearrange playlists on Android. A lot of complaints in the forum and they just don't bother answering.

PRECEDENTS:

     spotify replied: Hi Joseph! We understand your frustration. Rest assured, we monitor all feedback in our Community. We'll post any updates there

[2751304] past customer: #Android #app still broken. Can't reorder #songs in #playlist .. #Spotify
     spotify replied: Hey again! Don't worry, our devs are constantly checking all feedback posted in our Community. Hopefully this is something we'll be able to implement in the future. Let us know if you need anything else

[1928888] past customer: Really wish you could sort playlists on the app by which ones you have/haven't downloaded. #Spotify
     spotify replied: Hi there! Nice idea, it's definitely something for the team to consider. We'll be sure to let them know it's something you'd like to see

[1211743] past customer: Spotify won't shuffle my playlists on my phone anymore nd it's annoying
     spotify replied: Hey! Don't worry, help's here. What phone model, operating system, and Spotify version are you using? We'll see what we can suggest

[1630505] past customer: has left Android and Chromebook users out in the cold for years. No rearranging playlists, a critical feature of any music player.
     spotify replied: Hey there, we hear you! Be sure to suggest your idea in our Community at <link> and get support from other users

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
Hi there! We understand your frustration. Our devs are constantly checking feedback posted in our Community, and we'll post any updates there. 🙌

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hi Marcio. Sorry you feel that way. No worries, we've already passed your feedback to the right team. You can also vote for that idea at <link> Give us a shout if you have questions

Return the JSON scores.
